text:
anya: quick heads-up — after rolling the int8 quant build for magnet30B-v2 i see reproducible divergence on our long-prefill smoke where the prefills contain ISO timestamps (e.g. 2026-03-20T14:02:00Z).

sam: which divergence? output tokens or kvcache mismatch? :thinking:

anya: kvcache index drift + one-token off-by-one in attention results. float32 run is clean. int8 only. short repro below.

devon: can you drop the repro steps? i'll try on a dedicated GPU later.

anya: repro (on dev rig):
```
# run with quant-int8 branch
./scripts/run_prefill_smoke.sh --model magnet30B-v2 --prefill-file tests/prefill_with_timestamps.txt --longctx 65536 --seed 42
```
logs show: `KVCACHE: idx_write=1024 idx_read=1023` followed by token misalignment in step 1025.

maria: do you have the exact diff that introduced the int8 kernel? any rotary/rescale change?

anya: bisect points to commit abc1234 (quant-int8-kernel + rotary-rescale tweak).

chris: hmm — rotary phase scaling + quant rounding could drift the predicted pos indices used to address cache. if poscalc quantized slightly differently we can end up writing to off-by-one slot.

anya: that's the hypothesis. interestingly the prefill tokens that include exact-digit timestamps make sequence lengths align such that the drift shows up predictably. random text doesn't always trigger.

devon: can you dump kvcache fingerprints for the failing case? small tool: `tools/dump_kv_fingerprint.py --run 20260320-14-02`

anya: done, attached snippet from run 20260320-14-02: 
```
[INFO] kvcache.fingerprint: step=1023 hash=0x7a2f3b id=slot_1023
[INFO] kvcache.fingerprint: step=1024 hash=0x9c1d00 id=slot_1024
[ERROR] kvcache.read_mismatch: wanted slot_1024 got slot_1023
```

sam: can you try forcing float pos calc on int8 run (temporary) to see if defect is in poscalc or write/read gluing?

anya: running that now: `export POSCALC_FP=1 && ./scripts/run_prefill_smoke.sh ...`

infra-bot: job queued on dedicated-gpu-3 (run id: rq-88421).

maria: if float poscalc fixes it then we know quant rounding is culprit. if not, maybe write/read ordering or a race. any repro with single-threaded kernel?

anya: float poscalc run currently passing (no mismatch in the short run).

chris: ok that narrows it. next step bisect inside quant-poscalc kernel. i can instrument quant kernel to log rounded pos values for the steps around 1020-1030.

devon: also check whether our RopE scaling factor (we added per-head rescale in commit abc1234) is being applied before or after the quantization clamp. ordering could change rounding.

anya: good call. i see in the kernel: `apply_quant -> apply_rescale` (i'll open a quick patch to flip order).

sam: small ask — open an issue with reproducer + links to the failing run and the dump. mark P1 for model bring-up.

anya: created issue #4267 with repro, logs, dump and float-run link. assigning to @chris and @devon.

chris: will add additional instrumentation and try flipping order. if that fixes, we should include a unit test that injects timestamp-heavy prefills.

maria: also add a perf guard — if we switch to float poscalc as band-aid, we need to measure perf regression. might be OK on Dedicated but not Hosted.

devon: i'll schedule a longer run overnight with seeded prefills to check for flaky false negatives.

anya: thanks. leaving the reproducer and small dataset at: s3://redwood-test-repro/magnet30b/timestamp-prefill/ (run id rq-88421).

sam: thumbs up :thumbsup: keep updates in the issue thread.

infra-bot: rq-88421 completed on dedicated-gpu-3, exit=0. artifacts: s3://redwood-artifacts/rq-88421/

anya: follow-up: chris's flip-order patch (PR #3482) removed the mismatch in the full long-prefill run. still running long soak to be sure.

chris: if soak passes, we'll backport hotswap to int8 branch and add a regression test that includes ISO timestamps, time strings, and numeric-heavy tokens to catch brittle rounding-triggered shifts.

maria: cool — also add a brief note in model-onboard checklist about including timestamp-heavy prompts in long-context smoke. avoids subtle regressions later.

anya: agreed. thanks all.
